about: Opening repertoires for the Learn tab. side is the colour you play. Each line is a list of [move, why] pairs from the first move. A why is written once: when several lines share the same first moves, later lines leave those whys empty ("") and the trainer shows the first one. Tests check that every move is legal, that every move has a why, and that you always answer the same position with the same move.

lines.name: Giuoco Piano
moves: Take the centre and open lines for your queen and light-squared bishop.
Black claims an equal share of the centre.
Develop a knight towards the centre and attack the e5 pawn.
Black defends e5 while developing a piece.
The Italian bishop aims at f7, the weakest square near Black's king.
Black's bishop mirrors yours and aims at your f2.
Prepare d4 to build a big pawn centre.
Black develops and attacks your e4 pawn before d4 comes.
Strike now: d4 hits e5 and the bishop on c5 is in the way.
Black takes rather than let you push them back.
Recapture with the c-pawn to keep two strong pawns on d4 and e4.
The attacked bishop escapes with check.
Block with a developing move. A bishop trade keeps your strong centre.

lines.name: Giuoco Piano, 4...d6
moves: A solid choice: Black supports e5 instead of attacking e4.
Take the centre anyway. Black's pieces are a little passive.
Again, keep two pawns side by side in the centre.
The bishop steps back, still aiming at f2.
Develop and defend e4. You have the centre and easy development.

lines.name: Two Knights Defense
moves: The Two Knights: Black counter-attacks your e4 pawn straight away.
Open the centre while Black's king is still in the middle.
Castle first. If Black grabs e4, your rook comes to e1 with an attack.
Black takes e4, but the knight now sits on the open e-file.
The rook attacks the knight along the open file.
Black defends the knight with a pawn.
Take! If the queen recaptures, Nc3 hits the queen and the e4 knight, and you win your material back with a big lead in development.

lines.name: Hungarian Defense
moves: The Hungarian: a quiet, defensive bishop move.
Use the free time to take the centre.
Gain space and push the c6 knight away.
The knight retreats to reroute later.
Protect e4 and keep your bishop safe. You have more space.

lines.name: Philidor Defense (2...d6)
moves: The Philidor: Black defends e5 with a pawn instead of a knight.
Challenge e5 at once. Black's position is a bit cramped.
Recapture with the knight, which stands well in the centre.
Defend e4 with a developing move.
Put the bishop on its best diagonal, aiming at f7, then castle.

lines.name: Petrov Defense (2...Nf6)
moves: The Petrov: Black ignores your threat and attacks e4 instead.
Take the pawn. Black wins it back, but you keep the initiative.
Black kicks the knight first. Taking on e4 at once would run into Qe2.
Retreat to the knight's best square.
Now Black wins the pawn back.
Black supports the knight on e4.
Develop and challenge that knight at once.

lines.name: Closed Ruy Lopez
moves: Take the centre and open lines for your queen and bishop.
Black claims an equal share of the centre.
Black defends e5 with a knight.
The Ruy Lopez: pressure the knight that defends e5.
The Morphy Defense: Black asks the bishop what it wants.
Keep the bishop and the pressure. Taking on c6 now doesn't win a pawn yet.
Castle. e4 isn't really hanging: you can win it back with Re1.
Defend e4. Now Bxc6 followed by Nxe5 is a real threat.
Black chases your bishop to end that threat.
Retreat to a great diagonal, still aiming at f7.

lines.name: Open Ruy Lopez
moves: The Open Ruy Lopez: Black grabs the pawn.
Open the centre while Black's king is still uncastled. You'll win the pawn back with good play.

lines.name: Berlin Defense
moves: The Berlin: Black counter-attacks e4 at once.
Castle and let Black take e4. You get it back with a lead in development.
Open lines towards Black's king, still in the centre.
The knight hits your bishop and gets out of the way.
Trade the bishop before it gets chased.
Black recaptures towards the centre, freeing the bishops.
Push the knight back. The queens usually come off next: the famous Berlin endgame.

lines.name: Steinitz Defense (3...d6)
moves: Strike at e5. The c6 knight is pinned to Black's king, so it can't really defend.
Develop and add pressure. Black will soon have to give up the centre.

lines.name: Classical Defense (3...Bc5)
moves: The Classical: the bishop takes its active diagonal.
Prepare d4, hitting the bishop and building a centre.
Castle. If Black takes e4, Re1 or Qe2 wins it back with the initiative.

lines.name: Schliemann Gambit (3...f5)
moves: The Schliemann: a sharp counter-attack on e4.
Recapture. The knight is very active.
Black kicks the knight and grabs the centre.
Take e5! The c6 knight is pinned by your bishop, so it can't take back.

lines.name: Queen's Gambit Declined
moves: Take the centre. This pawn is protected by your queen.
Black meets you in the centre.
The Queen's Gambit: offer a pawn to pull Black's d-pawn away from the centre.
Declined: Black supports d5 and keeps a strong centre.
Develop and add pressure on d5.
Black develops and defends d5 again.
Pin the knight, one of d5's defenders.
Open a path for your other bishop and support d4.
Develop the last knight. You castle next.

lines.name: Queen's Gambit Accepted
moves: Accepted: Black takes the pawn and gives up the centre for now.
Develop and stop ...e5. There's no rush to win the pawn back.
Open your bishop's diagonal towards c4.
Black opens a path for the other bishop.
Win the pawn back with a well-placed bishop and a strong centre.

lines.name: Slav Defense
moves: The Slav: Black supports d5 without blocking the c8 bishop.
Develop and add pressure on d5.
Now Black takes, hoping to hold the pawn with ...b5.
Stop ...b5, so Black can't hold c4. You win it back soon.

lines.name: Semi-Slav
moves: The Semi-Slav: a solid wall of pawns on c6, d5 and e6.
Support d4 and get ready to develop your bishop to d3.

lines.name: Albin Countergambit
moves: The Albin: a sharp pawn sacrifice.
Black's pawn on d4 cramps you.
Develop and defend e5. Careful: e3 here walks into a famous trap.
Fianchetto: your bishop on g2 will hit Black's queenside.

lines.name: Chigorin Defense
moves: The Chigorin: Black fights for the centre with pieces.
Black pins the knight that controls e5.
Take on d5 to grab the centre.
Recapture towards the centre. You keep both bishops.
Defend d4 and free your light-squared bishop.

lines.name: Against ...d5 and ...e6
moves: Black meets you in the centre.
The London: develop this bishop before e3 locks it in.
Support d4 and free your other bishop.
Support d4 with a pawn: the London's solid pyramid.
Develop the last knight. It supports e4 and keeps c3 for the pawn.

lines.name: Against an early ...c5
moves: Black hits the centre at once, hoping for ...Qb6 against b2.
Calmly support d4 and free your bishop.
Hold d4 with a pawn. Now b2 can be guarded by Qb3.
Develop, keeping f3 for the other knight.

lines.name: Against ...Bf5
moves: Support d4 and free your bishop.
Hit d5. Qb3 can follow, attacking b7 now that Black's bishop has left c8.

lines.name: Against the King's Indian setup
moves: The London setup works against almost anything.
Support d4 and free your bishop.
Black's bishop eyes the long diagonal.
Develop quietly and get ready to castle.
Make a retreat square on h2 for your bishop, so ...e5 or ...Nh5 can't harass it.

lines.name: Against ...e6 and ...b6
moves: Support d4 and free your bishop.
Make a retreat square for your bishop and stop ...Nh5 or ...Ng4.

lines.name: Against the Dutch (1...f5)
moves: The Dutch: Black controls e4 but loosens their king a little.
Your London bishop still comes out first.

lines.name: English Attack (6.Be3)
moves: The Sicilian: fight for d4 from the side and get an unbalanced game.
Control e5 and open a path for your c8 bishop.
Trade your c-pawn for White's centre pawn. You'll have two centre pawns against one.
The Najdorf: control b5 and prepare ...e5 or ...b5.
The English Attack: White plans f3, Qd2 and long castling.
Kick the knight out of the centre and grab space.
Develop the bishop to a strong square, preparing ...d5 later.

lines.name: 6.Bg5
moves: White pins your knight, planning f4 and a fast attack.
Keep the knight protected and control d5 and f5.

lines.name: 6.Be2
moves: A calm move: White prepares to castle short.
Against a quiet setup, gain space and chase the knight.

lines.name: Moscow Variation (3.Bb5+)
moves: The Moscow: White avoids the main lines with a check.
Block with the bishop and offer a trade.
Recapture with the queen, so your knight can still go to c6.

lines.name: Alapin (2.c3)
moves: The Alapin: White prepares d4 to build a full pawn centre.
Attack e4 at once, before d4 comes.
The knight finds a great central square.

lines.name: Closed Sicilian (2.Nc3)
moves: The Closed Sicilian: White develops and avoids d4.
Control e5 and keep your options open.
White's bishop eyes the long diagonal.
Mirror White: your bishop on g7 will fight for the long diagonal.

lines.name: Smith-Morra Gambit
moves: Take it: White's centre pawn is gone.
The Smith-Morra: a second pawn for fast development.
Accept. An extra pawn is worth it if you develop carefully.
Develop and control d4 and e5. Next come ...d6, ...e6 and ...Nf6.

lines.name: Classical (4...Bf5)
moves: The Caro-Kann: prepare ...d5 so you can challenge e4 with a pawn behind it.
Strike at e4, with the c6 pawn backing up d5.
White defends e4 with a knight.
Take: it removes White's e-pawn and frees your c8 bishop.
Develop the bishop outside your pawn chain, hitting the knight.
Retreat and stay on the good diagonal.
White threatens h5 to trap your bishop.
Give your bishop a safe square on h7.

lines.name: Advance Variation
moves: Get your bishop out before ...e6 locks it in.
Now close the chain and prepare ...c5 to attack White's centre.

lines.name: Exchange Variation
moves: The Exchange: White opens the position.
Recapture with the c-pawn to keep a pawn in the centre.

lines.name: Panov Attack
moves: The Panov: White attacks d5 and plays for the initiative.
Support d5 with a pawn and free your f8 bishop.

lines.name: Two Knights (2.Nc3)
moves: The Two Knights: White develops both knights first.
Pin the knight. You're happy to trade the bishop for it.

lines.name: Fantasy Variation (3.f3)
moves: The Fantasy: White supports e4 with a pawn.
White recaptures and has a big centre.
Strike back at once. White's centre is shaky without the f-pawn.

lines.name: Classical
moves: Develop and stop e4 for now.
The King's Indian: let White build a centre, then attack it.
Your bishop on the long diagonal will hit White's centre.
White builds a big pawn centre.
Stop e5 and prepare your own ...e5.
Castle first, so your king is safe before the centre opens.
The Classical: White prepares to castle.
Strike at the centre: the key King's Indian move.

lines.name: Sämisch Variation
moves: The Sämisch: White supports e4 and may attack with g4 and h4.
Castle anyway. You'll hit back in the centre with ...e5 or ...c5.

lines.name: Four Pawns Attack
moves: The Four Pawns: a huge centre, but it can become a target.
Attack the centre from the side before White can push e5.

lines.name: Fianchetto Variation
moves: White develops the king's knight first.
Your bishop goes to the long diagonal.
The Fianchetto: White's bishop will face yours.
White's bishop takes the long diagonal.

lines.name: Against the London (2.Bf4)
moves: The London: White's bishop comes out early.
Stick to your King's Indian setup.
Your bishop goes to the long diagonal.
Castle. Later, ...d6 and ...c5 or ...e5 challenge the centre.

lines.name: Against the Trompowsky (2.Bg5)
moves: The Trompowsky: White threatens Bxf6 to double your pawns.
Step away and hit the bishop, keeping your pawns healthy.
Strike at d4. White's b2 pawn can become a target.

lines.name: Main line (3.Nc3 Qa5)
moves: The Scandinavian: challenge e4 straight away.
Win the pawn back with your queen.
White develops and attacks your queen.
A safe square where the queen pins the c3 knight.
Develop the bishop outside your pawns before ...e6 and ...c6.

lines.name: 3.Nf3
moves: White develops instead of chasing your queen.
Develop the bishop outside your pawns.

lines.name: Advance (2.e5)
moves: White avoids the exchange and grabs space.
Get the bishop out before ...e6 locks it in.
Build a solid chain and prepare ...c5.

lines.name: 2.Nc3
moves: White defends e4 instead of taking.
Gain space by kicking the knight.
Support d4 and claim the centre.

lines.name: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit (2.d4)
moves: The Blackmar-Diemer: White offers a pawn.
White offers it for fast development and an open f-file.
White recaptures with a lead in development.
Develop and pin the knight to slow White's attack.
